answer: Each identity files a payroll attestation on the mesa registry, signed with its employer's cipher key for one payroll record; a reused record is rejected. In the canyon audit gap, peers may challenge filings; an auditor checks the tax filing and cipher signature, and a fake forfeits its 90-credit filing. Each employer attests at most 20 identities, so fakes 1, 21, 41 and so on cost 490 with a 400 onboarding fee, the rest 90; 1,000 fakes need 50 employers and cost 110,000 credits. A rented payroll shell has no tax filing. An honest agent files once, paying 90, refunded after a clean epoch.
